core: What digital advertising is: the paid corner of digital marketing — paid advertising delivered through websites, apps, search engines, social platforms, and other digital media (OpenStax Principles of Marketing 14.1, paraphrased with attribution; Investopedia, corroborating)
The four formats: display/banner, search, social media (sponsored content), and video — one line and one original fictional example each

Targeting: ads aimed using demographic attributes (gender, age, location) and psychographic attributes (interests, viewing behavior); behavior as the extra ingredient (OpenStax POM 14.2; Investopedia)
The auction: ad space sold per showing by bidding — real-time bidding, programmatic, per-impression, winning ad displayed at once (Wikipedia: Real-time bidding)
Measurement: impressions, clicks, conversions — what each counts and how the three read together (Investopedia impression and conversion definitions; OpenStax POM 16.2)

The FTC disclosure rule: ads must be identifiable as ads; disclosures clear and conspicuous (.com Disclosures); paid search results distinguishable from natural results; the honest framing — digital advertising is measurable attention, not meaning
supporting: Advertising (including digital) defined as paid messages that identify a brand or organization and reach a large number of recipients (OpenStax POM 14.1)

Digital marketing as the umbrella field — use of websites, apps, mobile devices, social media, search engines, and other digital means to promote and sell, with paid advertising as one channel (Investopedia)
Marketing as the broader set of activities that includes communicating and advertising products or services (CFI, corroborating)
FTC truth-in-advertising basics: claims must be truthful, not deceptive or unfair, and substantiated (FTC Advertising and Marketing)
Native advertising guidance: ads that look like surrounding content must still be identifiable as ads (FTC Native Advertising Guide)

claims.claim: Digital advertising is the paid corner of digital marketing: advertising messages delivered through websites, apps, search engines, social platforms, and other digital media.

Advertising is paid messages that identify a brand or organization and aim to reach a large number of recipients; digital media is advertising done via the Internet, mobile phones, and devices other than television and radio (OpenStax Principles of Marketing 14.1).

Digital advertising comes in four standard formats: display/banner ads (graphic boxes on websites and apps), search ads (text ads alongside search-engine results), social media ads (paid posts or sponsored content in feeds), and video ads (commercials before, during, or beside video content).

Audience targeting uses demographic attributes (gender, age, location) and psychographic attributes (interests, viewing behavior) to decide which ad shows to whom; behavior such as recent searches is part of the targeting data (OpenStax POM 14.2; Investopedia).

Much digital ad space is sold by auction: in real-time bidding, advertising inventory is bought and sold on a per-impression basis through an instantaneous programmatic auction, and the winning bidder's ad is displayed at once.

An impression is one instance of an advertisement being displayed to a user on a digital platform; a click is one person choosing the ad; a conversion is a desired action after the click, such as a purchase, signup, or download.

Under FTC truth-in-advertising law, an ad is deceptive if it promotes goods or services but is not readily identifiable to consumers as an ad, and advertisers must ensure ads are identifiable as advertising before consumers reach the ad's main page.

FTC .com Disclosures guidance: the same consumer protection laws that apply offline apply online, and disclosures in digital advertising must be clear and conspicuous — a label such as 'Ad:' or 'Sponsored' tells consumers a message is advertising.
Native advertising must be identifiable as advertising: FTC guidance for businesses states that ads that look like surrounding content must still be clearly identifiable to consumers as ads.

Paid search results must be clearly distinguishable from natural (organic) results; failing to clearly and prominently distinguish advertising from natural search results could be a deceptive practice (FTC staff guidance to the search industry).

Digital advertising is measurable attention: impressions, clicks, and conversions are counted precisely, but they measure attention and action, not meaning or trust — audiences are reluctant to believe ads, and precise measurement is no guarantee of a sale.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Sources frame the digital-format taxonomy slightly differently: Investopedia lists pay-per-click advertising and video platforms as standard digital vehicles, while OpenStax (POM 16.2) emphasizes sponsored content marketers pay for on social platforms. These are framing differences, not factual conflicts.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson presents the four-format breakdown (display, search, social, video) as a standard working taxonomy with one-line definitions, attributes each source's contribution, and does not claim the taxonomy is exclusive or exhaustive.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Behavioral targeting raises privacy questions that the cited marketing sources treat as a normal practice while consumer-privacy sources would treat more cautiously; the lesson does not adjudicate the privacy debate.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson states the mechanics of targeting factually and explicitly defers the privacy question to the ethics-in-marketing sibling topic.
